ECG-EKG (Electrocardiograph)

Electronics, as in many other fields, is a key component in the medical field as well. In the diagnosis and treatment process, electronic medical devices are indispensable tools for doctors. Imaging systems, surgical robots, analytical devices, and many other types of electronic setups serve medicine. This makes electronics essential for medicine. Consequently, medical science provides a broad area of study for electronics, and the electronics market finds a lucrative sector in medicine. In this post, I will talk about the EKG project we implemented during my university years.

What is EKG?

An EKG is a waveform that observes the electrical activity of the heart (such as rhythm, frequency, the pattern of heartbeats, propagation, and repolarization) graphically through electrodes attached to the skin. The device that allows us to examine this signal is called an EKG machine. It holds a very valuable place in medicine.

How Does It Work?

This device, developed to examine the functioning of the heart, essentially works by adapting the sounds produced during the contraction and relaxation of the heart. It is based on converting the sound signals, received by the microphones in the attached electrodes, into electrical signals that can be observed.

Acquiring the EKG Signal

The heart generates very low amplitude electrical and sound signals as it contracts and relaxes. When designing the EKG device, we amplify these signals and transfer them to a monitor or a medium where we can observe them. There are many methods to obtain an EKG graph. We used the three-lead method.

In measurements taken from two arms and one leg, we get the difference between the two arms and compare it with the reference point on the leg to obtain the EKG signal. The signals are carried to the signal amplifier through coaxial cables with electrodes attached to the arms and one leg. We performed the differential amplification using an instrumentation amplifier. Many projects and books in the market use the AD624 integrated circuit for the first stage differential process, but this IC can be difficult to find in Turkey. Instead, we designed our own instrumentation amplifier. Designing an instrumentation amplifier is not as difficult as it might seem. It can be done with a few operational amplifiers and some resistors (in its simplest form).

When we examine the amplified differential signal, we will see that it consists of many overlapping signals. To obtain the EKG signal, we need to eliminate the other signals. We designed a band-pass filter to remove the other signals. The central frequency of the band-pass filter must match the frequency of our EKG signal, otherwise, we would also filter out the EKG signal.

After performing these steps, if we take an output, we will encounter a surprise. We will see that the 50Hz mains frequency is superimposed on our EKG signal. To eliminate this, we used a notch filter. A notch filter is essentially a band-stop filter that suppresses the 50Hz frequency while allowing all other frequencies to pass. We must adjust our notch filter very carefully and avoid extending the cut-off points. Otherwise, it may also suppress our EKG signal.

Here is the screen capture of the ISIS diagram of the circuit we designed to acquire, filter, and amplify the EKG signal.

I wanted to share with you some images from our work environment and some outputs we obtained during our studies.

  • Image 1: Materials used in the making of the EKG. As seen, it’s just a handful of components.
  • Image 2: The printed circuit board of our EKG device.
  • Image 3: The first test run of our circuit on the board.
  • Image 4 and result: Our output signal as shown in the image.

Lastly, we amplified our EKG signal and got an output on the oscilloscope screen. If we prefer a graphical screen instead of an oscilloscope, we need to pass our signal through an AD converter. Writing a few lines of code and using a PIC16F877 will suffice for this process. Although this study was not done professionally, we managed to obtain a signal very close to the real one. The operation of professional EKG devices is fundamentally similar to the above but involves more complex and powerful stages to achieve more precise results.

Note

This is a project from a course during my undergraduate studies and the content may have become outdated.
